texts.home.story.title: The hand behind the wonder
texts.home.story.p1: Jadugar Rajtilak belongs to the old school of Indian stage magic — satin and spotlights, doves and disappearances — rebuilt with the pacing of modern cinema. Twelve years and more than five hundred shows later, the mission has not changed: make an entire hall stop breathing at the same instant.
texts.home.story.p2: Every evening is engineered for its room. A sangeet gets warmth and participation, a corporate annual day gets precision to the run-sheet, a college fest gets scale the back row can feel. What never changes is the refusal to perform anything the cheapest seat cannot see.

texts.about.hero.sub: The story behind the vermilion mark — craft, milestones and the standard every Rajtilak show answers to.
texts.about.story.title: The story so far
texts.about.story.p1: Jadugar Rajtilak stepped onto a stage for the first time at a school function — and discovered that a room full of strangers falling silent together is the most addictive sound in theatre. What began as card tricks at family gatherings became twelve years of staged performances across more than forty cities.
texts.about.story.p2: The craft sits at the intersection of sleight-of-hand, stagecraft and audience psychology. Every Rajtilak show is rebuilt for its room: the wedding sangeet needs warmth, the corporate annual day needs precision to a run-sheet, the college fest needs scale. The constant is a refusal to perform anything the back row cannot see or the front row cannot feel.
texts.about.story.p3: Off stage, the practice is unglamorous and deliberate — rehearsing timings to a metronome, building props by hand, and retiring an effect the moment it stops surprising the performer. That is the standard a Rajtilak audience is paying for.

texts.about.milestones.title: The road to the royal stage
texts.about.milestone1: The first stage — a school function, a borrowed deck, and a hall that would not stop clapping.
texts.about.milestone2: The referral chain — the first corporate annual day that quietly booked the next three.
texts.about.milestone3: Wedding seasons — hundreds of sangeets, receptions and cocktail evenings across the country.
texts.about.milestone4: The Grand production — full crew, projection design and the large-format illusion act.
texts.about.philosophy.title: Three rules the act answers to
texts.about.philosophy.sub: The same principles decide which effects make the set — and which are retired.
texts.about.philosophy1t: The back row is the client
texts.about.philosophy1d: If it cannot read from the last seat, it does not go on the rider. Scale, light and timing are engineered for the cheapest seat in the house.
texts.about.philosophy2d: Astonishment without humiliation. Volunteers leave the stage taller than they arrived — the host is thanked, never trapped.
texts.about.philosophy3d: Metronome-timed pacing, scored transitions, contingency choreography for prop failure. Magic is a stagecraft discipline first.

texts.faq.hero.title: Everything hosts ask before booking
texts.faq.hero.sub: Pricing, travel, technical riders, safety and cancellation — answered plainly. Anything else, the studio replies within a working day.
texts.faq.q1: How much does a show cost?
texts.faq.a1: Pricing is shared as a written quote after your enquiry — it depends on city, duration, guest count and staging, and every quote states travel and technical requirements up front with no hidden line items. Share your date and occasion to receive the exact figure in writing.
texts.faq.q2: Do you travel to other cities?
texts.faq.a2: Yes. Travel within Udaipur and across Rajasthan is included in most tiers; outside travel is quoted as actuals (fare + stay) and confirmed in writing before booking. Availability can be checked live on the booking calendar before you enquire.
texts.faq.q3: What technical setup do you need?
texts.faq.a3: A stage area of roughly 12×10 ft, a basic sound system with two microphones, and general stage lighting. The Royal and Grand tiers include a full technical rider, and the team coordinates directly with your venue or DJ.
texts.faq.q4: Is the show safe for children?
texts.faq.a4: The birthday tier is age-calibrated: no fire, no darkness, no frightening content. Effects are colour-forward and participatory, and the birthday child stars in the finale. Parents are welcome to film the entire act.
texts.faq.a5: Cancellations 30+ days before the show receive a full refund of any advance; within 30 days, the advance is adjusted against a rescheduled date within 12 months. Full terms are on the Legal page and confirmed in the booking contract.
texts.faq.q6: How far ahead should we book?
texts.faq.a6: Peak wedding and festive season dates typically close 6–8 weeks ahead. The booking calendar shows live availability, and an enquiry reserves a soft-hold on your date for 72 hours while the quote is prepared.
texts.faq.q7: How does a booking actually come together, step by step?
texts.faq.a7: Every booking follows the same four steps: check your date on the live calendar, enquire with your occasion details, receive a written quote (with a 72-hour soft-hold on your evening while you decide), then confirm with an advance and a clear contract. Between confirmation and showtime the team coordinates directly with your venue, DJ or planner so nothing is left to the day itself.
texts.faq.q8: Can the act be customised to our occasion?
texts.faq.a8: Yes — customisation is built into the craft, not an add-on. Wedding routines are woven around the couple's story, corporate acts are scripted to the brand and the run-sheet, and the birthday child always stars in the finale. The private tier even begins with a planning call to curate the set-list for your guest list. Share the occasion when you enquire and the routine is dressed for it.
texts.faq.q9: Can our guests film and photograph the show?
texts.faq.a9: Yes — families and guests are welcome to film. The birthday tier explicitly invites parents to film the entire act, and many of the most-shared frames in the gallery were taken by guests at their tables. If your event has an official photographer or videographer, the team coordinates the angles in advance so staged lighting and camera flashes work together instead of against each other.
